name: Cursor
tagline: AI-first code editor built on VS Code
description: Cursor is an AI code editor with codebase-aware chat, tab completion, and agent modes for multi-file edits. Strong fit for daily software development. Since November 5, 2026, cloud agents on paid plans can also build and publish live apps: Cursor scaffolds the web app, sets up a Postgres database if needed, adds sign-in behind Cursor SSO, runs security checks, and hosts it at a link you choose.
pricingNote: Free plan with limited agent requests; Plus $8 a month (Grok models only), Premium $30, Super $100, and Ultra $200 a month; Teams from $30 per user a month; third-party models billed at API list price

name: Claude
tagline: Anthropic assistant for reasoning, writing, and code
description: Claude is Anthropic's AI assistant known for long-context analysis, careful writing, and strong coding help across chat and projects. On November 9, 2026, Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2, its most capable model for demanding technical work in coding, finance, and the sciences. Fable 5.2 has a 1M-token context window, generates output up to 30% faster than Fable 5.1, and costs less on the API at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens (down from $10 and $50). In the Claude apps it is available on the paid Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, and Enterprise plans from the model picker, and it is also in Claude Code and Cowork. On November 10, 2026, Anthropic added Claude Whiteboards (a shared board Claude turns into timelines and action items) and Claude Sheets (spreadsheets with tabs, formulas, and drop-downs that Claude builds and edits with you) in beta on all paid plans, made Claude Data generally available, and launched Claude Meetings in beta on Team and Enterprise plans, which adds Claude to Google Meet calls as a visible participant.
pricingNote: Free plan; Pro is $20 per month ($17 a month billed annually), Max is $100 per month, and the new Ultra plan is $200 per month; Team and Enterprise plans for organizations

name: ChatGPT
tagline: OpenAI's flagship conversational AI
description: ChatGPT is OpenAI's general-purpose assistant for chat, writing, coding, image generation, and browsing. Broadest everyday AI starting point. As of November 4, 2026, Images 2.6 is available in ChatGPT, Codex, and the API, with GIF support and faster image edits.
pricingNote: Free plan for everyone; Go, Plus, and Pro plans for individuals and Business (from 2 users) and Enterprise plans for companies, all priced per user a month on chatgpt.com/pricing

name: Gemini
tagline: Google's multimodal AI across web and Workspace
description: Gemini is Google's AI assistant with deep Google ecosystem ties, multimodal understanding, and strong research workflows. On November 10, 2026, Google released Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model, built for long, multi-step work such as complex coding and debugging, dense document analysis, and scientific research; it uses more tokens than Gemini 4 Argon to reason and verify, while Argon remains Google's pick for most everyday work. Carbon is rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search, and Google Antigravity, and it is on the Gemini API paid tier at an introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens until November 30, 2026, then $4 and $20.
pricingNote: Free with a Google account; Google AI Plus is $4.99, Google AI Pro $19.99, and Google AI Ultra from $99.99 per month (US prices)

name: GitHub Copilot
tagline: AI pair programmer inside your IDE and GitHub
description: GitHub Copilot suggests code as you type, answers questions in the IDE, and helps with pull requests across popular editors.
pricingNote: Copilot Free with limited use; Pro $10, Pro+ $39, and Max $100 a month; Business $19 and Enterprise $39 per seat a month

name: Midjourney
tagline: Artistic AI image generation
description: Midjourney generates high-quality artistic images from text prompts, widely used for concept art, marketing visuals, and exploration.
pricingNote: Subscription only: Basic $10, Standard $30, Pro $60, and Mega $120 a month, or 20% less billed yearly ($8, $24, $48, and $96 a month); Standard and above include unlimited Relax mode image generations; companies with more than $1M in yearly revenue need Pro or Mega

name: Perplexity
tagline: AI search engine with cited answers
description: Perplexity answers questions with live web sources and citations, useful when you need research you can verify. On November 6, 2026 it added Teammates for Max subscribers on the web: personal agents that take an ongoing job, plan the work, run tasks in parallel, and follow through until results are ready for review. Each teammate can use your Computer tasks, skills, memory, and tools, work with other teammates, and message coworkers in Slack. Computer can also run fully on-device on supported Apple-silicon Macs for Pro, Max, and Enterprise subscribers (Mac app 26.42.0 or later, 36 GB of unified memory recommended), so with your permission it can work across local files and Mac apps such as Notes and Mail without sending that personal data to the cloud.
bestFor: private local Computer tasks on a Mac
pricingNote: Free Standard plan; paid Pro and Max plans on perplexity.ai, plus Education Pro at $10 per month for verified students and educators

name: ElevenLabs
tagline: AI voice synthesis and cloning
description: ElevenLabs creates natural text-to-speech, voice clones, and dubbing for podcasts, products, and video.
pricingNote: Free plan with 10,000 credits a month and no commercial license; Starter is $6 per month and adds a commercial license, Creator $22, and Pro $99; Scale and Business plans for teams

name: Runway
tagline: AI video generation and editing
description: Runway offers generative video and image models plus editing tools for filmmakers, marketers, and creators producing short clips from text or images. Plans are credit-based across Gen-4.5 and partner models, with App Studio and Runway Ads on paid tiers.
pricingNote: Free with 125 one-time credits; Standard $12 a month billed yearly ($15 monthly) with 625 credits; Pro $28 a month billed yearly ($35 monthly) with 2,250 credits; Max $76 a month billed yearly ($95 monthly) with 9,500 credits; extra credits from 1,000 minimum; see runway.com/pricing

name: Claude Code
tagline: Anthropic's agentic coding in the terminal
description: Claude Code is Anthropic's terminal-native coding agent for reading repos, making edits, and running tasks with Claude models.
pricingNote: Uses Claude subscription or API; see Anthropic docs

name: OpenAI Codex
tagline: OpenAI's open-source coding agent for your terminal
description: OpenAI Codex is OpenAI's coding agent. The open-source Codex CLI reads your repo, edits files, and runs commands inside a sandbox with permission controls, and you can sign in with ChatGPT or use an API key. Version 0.167.0 (November 6, 2026) added an agent command center (codex agents) that marks unread results, switching between connected backends without losing your draft, local image previews while you compose, Google Cloud Vertex AI setup during sign-in, and expandable patch details inside approval prompts. GPT-6.1 Sol became its default model in version 0.161.0 on October 7.
bestFor: managing several agent sessions from one command center
pricingNote: Sign in with a ChatGPT plan or use an OpenAI API key; see openai.com/codex for plan details

name: Google Antigravity
tagline: Google's agentic coding platform across App, CLI, IDE, and SDK
description: Google Antigravity is an agentic coding platform for building with AI agents across an app, CLI, IDE, and SDK. Aimed at developers who want agent-driven workflows inside Google's AI stack. Since November 10, 2026, Google AI Ultra subscribers can use Gemini 4 Carbon, Google's strongest model, in Antigravity, and Google is previewing /swarm, which turns one prompt into a coordinated team of agents working in parallel isolated workspaces that you can track in real time.
pricingNote: Free for individuals with rate limits; Google AI Pro and Ultra unlock more capacity

name: Grok
tagline: xAI assistant with real-time X awareness
description: Grok is xAI's assistant available on x.ai and X, oriented toward real-time information and a more direct conversational style.
pricingNote: Free to try on grok.com and in the apps; paid plans are sold through The X Subscription: Plus $8, Premium $30, Super $100, and Ultra $200 a month (less billed yearly); existing SuperGrok and X Premium plans continue

name: v0
tagline: Vercel's AI UI generator for React
description: v0 by Vercel generates UI components and full pages from prompts, geared toward Next.js and modern React stacks.
pricingNote: Free plan with a 7 message per day limit and deploys to Vercel; Plus starts at $30 per user per month and Business is $100 per user per month

name: Lovable
tagline: Build full-stack apps from natural language
description: Lovable turns prompts into working web apps with UI and backend scaffolding, aimed at rapid product prototyping.
pricingNote: Free plan with 5 build credits a day (up to 30 a month); paid Pro and Business plans add monthly credits, see lovable.dev/pricing

name: Bolt.new
tagline: In-browser AI app builder by StackBlitz
description: Bolt.new lets you prompt, edit, and run full-stack web apps in the browser with StackBlitz's WebContainers.
pricingNote: Free plan with 1M tokens a month and website hosting; Pro from $25 a month and Teams from $30 a month, billed monthly; Enterprise is custom

name: Wix Studio Two
tagline: AI-native visual site builder that exports real React code
description: Wix Studio Two, announced November 2, 2026, is an AI-native version of the Wix Studio visual editor for agencies and developers. Its built-in agent, Aria 2.0, can generate full sites, sections, pages, images, and custom React components from a prompt, and teams can save repeatable steps as Skills. You can export a site as a standard React project, keep working on it in Claude, Codex, Cursor, or any IDE, and import it back into the visual editor. It also includes a browser-based VS Code environment and MCP-powered capabilities that let AI agents manage Wix business features such as Stores and Bookings. It is rolling out to Wix Partners first, then gradually to all users.
bestFor: visual editing plus real React code
pricingNote: Rolling out to Wix Partners first, then gradually to all users; Wix Studio site plans are listed on wix.com/studio/plans

name: Spacefast
tagline: Automattic's publishing home for apps and sites your AI builds, with a live link in the chat
description: Spacefast is a new company from Automattic, the team behind WordPress.com, launched on November 9, 2026. It is not an AI builder itself: you keep working in Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or another agent, and Spacefast gives that agent building instructions, a database, and hosting, then returns a live link right in the chat. Each project gets its own Space that is private by default, saves a version with every change so you can roll back, and supports comments pinned on the page that your AI can turn into fixes. Spaces also include file uploads and built-in visitor stats. You can publish without an account, or use the drop.fast drag-and-drop page, Git pushes, or the npx spacefast CLI. It supports Next.js, TanStack Start, Astro, and PHP projects, and Automattic says app authentication, transactional email, and shared team knowledge are coming in the next few weeks.
bestFor: publishing what ChatGPT or Claude builds without setting up hosting
sharing private drafts and collecting comments on the page
small apps that need a ready database
pricingNote: Free to start with no card; Personal plans include $1 a month of usage, custom domains, and a database; Go is $5 a month and Pro is $15 a month per member; Enterprise is custom

name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
tagline: Cognition's agentic IDE and agent command center, formerly Windsurf
description: Devin Desktop is the new name for Windsurf, Cognition's AI IDE. It keeps the full Windsurf IDE with Supercomplete tab predictions, and adds an agent command center for running and reviewing many agents, locally or in Devin Cloud, using the Agent Client Protocol. Plans, extensions, and settings carry over from Windsurf, and Windsurf for JetBrains is still available. SWE-2 Flash launched November 4, 2026, and is available in Devin Desktop and the CLI at one-fifth the price and 3x the speed of SWE-2; Cognition says it is free through November 30, 2026 for eligible paid Devin plans (Pro, Max, and Teams).
bestFor: managing several coding agents in one place
pricingNote: Free $0; Pro $20 per month; Max $200 per month; Teams $80 per month plus $40 per full seat; Enterprise on request

name: OpenCode
tagline: Open source AI coding agent for terminal, IDE, and desktop
description: OpenCode is an open source coding agent that works in your terminal, IDE, or a desktop app and connects to 75+ model providers, including local models. OpenCode 2.0, announced October 12, 2026, added a shared background server for all clients, background subagents, a Code Mode for tool calls, and an embeddable SDK.
pricingNote: Free and open source; bring your own model provider or subscription, or use OpenCode Zen models

name: Cline
tagline: Open source coding agent for VS Code and the terminal
description: Cline is an open source AI coding agent that runs as a VS Code extension and a CLI. It plans and makes multi-file changes, runs commands, and uses MCP tools, with your own API keys or the Cline provider. Version 4.1.25 (October 16, 2026) began rolling out Cline Cloud sessions, which run a task in a hosted sandbox on a GitHub repo and branch you pick and keep going after you close your editor. It also retries interrupted provider responses up to 3 times and fixes timeouts on long local-model requests.
pricingNote: Free and open source for individual developers; pay only for AI inference with your own keys or Cline credits. Enterprise plan on cline.bot

name: Zed
tagline: Fast open source code editor with a built-in AI agent
description: Zed is a fast, open source code editor with an Agent Panel, edit predictions, and support for external agents such as Claude Agent and Codex CLI through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). Zed 1.27.0 (November 4, 2026) writes AI commit messages in the style of your three most recent commits, cuts Agent Panel memory and CPU use on long threads, and speeds up the Git Graph. It also removed agent checkpoints (reject edits or use Git to undo) and now requires macOS 12 Monterey or later. Zed ships weekly releases.
bestFor: running external coding agents in one editor
pricingNote: Personal plan is $0 with your own API keys or external agents; Pro is $10 per month with $5 of tokens; Business is $30 per seat per month

name: Kiro
tagline: AWS's spec-driven agentic IDE, CLI, and web agent
description: Kiro is an agentic coding tool built and operated by AWS. It turns prompts into requirements, designs, and task lists (specs), then implements them with parallel agents, and checks behavior with property-based tests. It runs as an IDE that supports Open VSX extensions and VS Code settings, a CLI, and Kiro Web, and works with MCP, AGENTS.md, and the Agent Client Protocol. Recent releases added Memory across chat sessions in the IDE (October 19, 2026), workspace trust in the CLI (October 20), and MCP tools that can pause to ask for input plus Claude Haiku 5.5 support (October 23). You do not need an AWS account to use it. On November 5, 2026 AWS made Kiro bots generally available in Kiro Crew, its open source workspace: named, long-running agents with their own memory and workspace that run and monitor parallel sessions and can work on a schedule.
bestFor: parallel agents from plan to PR
teams that want AWS-grade admin controls
pricingNote: Free tier with 50 credits; Pro is $20, Pro+ $40, Pro Max $100, and Power $200 per user per month; add-on credits $0.04 each

name: Replit Agent
tagline: AI agent that builds and deploys in Replit
description: Replit Agent helps you create, run, and deploy apps inside Replit from natural language instructions.
pricingNote: Part of Replit paid plans: Core is $20 per month ($18 billed annually) and Pro is $100 per month ($90 billed annually); Enterprise is custom

name: Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM)
tagline: Google's source-grounded research notebook
description: Gemini Notebook, called NotebookLM until Google renamed it on July 16, 2026, lets you upload sources and chat with them, generate briefs, and create Audio Overviews grounded in your documents. Notebooks sync with the Gemini app, and Google is rolling out a secure cloud computer in every notebook that writes and runs code to analyze data in your sources, starting with Google AI Ultra and coming to Pro users on the web.
pricingNote: Free with a Google account; higher limits on Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra plans, and included in Google Workspace plans

name: Consensus
tagline: AI search across scientific papers
description: Consensus searches academic papers and summarizes findings so you can see what research says on a question.
pricingNote: Free plan with unlimited paper searches; Pro is $20 per month ($12 billed annually) and Deep is $65 per month ($45 billed annually)

name: Elicit
tagline: AI research assistant for literature review
description: Elicit helps researchers find papers, extract data into tables, and speed up systematic literature review workflows.
pricingNote: Free Basic plan with unlimited paper search and summaries; Pro is $49 and Scale $229 per user per month, billed annually

name: SciSpace
tagline: AI research agent for literature reviews and papers
description: SciSpace is an AI research workspace built around SciSpace Agent, which searches the literature, summarizes and compares papers, and drafts reports and manuscript sections from the papers you pick. It also has a Citation Verifier that checks whether your sources support your claims. Agent tasks run on monthly credits, and since October 9, 2026 the Advanced and Max plans include unlimited agent usage with fair-use limits.
bestFor: checking that citations support your claims
pricingNote: Basic is $0 with 100 credits per month; Premium is $20 per month ($12 billed annually); Advanced is $90 ($70 billed annually) and Max $200 ($160 billed annually), both with unlimited agent usage under fair-use limits

name: Scholarcy
tagline: AI summaries and flashcards for academic papers
description: Scholarcy summarizes research papers, articles, textbook chapters, and videos into interactive flashcards that pull out key findings, concepts, and contributions. It highlights important sections, points to related reading, stores references, figures, and tables in a searchable library, imports from Zotero, and exports to citation managers, Excel, and note apps, including one-click bibliographies in Word.
bestFor: building a library of research notes
pricingNote: Free plan limited to 10 summaries (free Article Summarizer allows 1 per day); paid subscription unlocks unlimited summaries, see scholarcy.com/pricing

name: Elorian Glimpse
tagline: Visual reasoning model for images and video
description: Glimpse is Elorian's first model, launched October 16, 2026 as a research preview. It reasons over images and video by zooming into regions, rewatching clips at denser frame rates, and running code to measure what it sees.
pricingNote: API listed at $0.60 per 1M input and $3 per 1M output tokens; chat UI also available

name: Muse Wonder
tagline: Meta's frontier model for coding, agents, and computer use
description: Muse Wonder is Meta's most capable model, launched October 12, 2026 in preview on the Meta Model API and in Muse Code. It is built for complex software engineering and long-running agents, takes text, image, video, audio, and PDF input, and has a 1M token context window.
pricingNote: API listed at $4 per 1M input and $20 per 1M output tokens; Muse Wonder Full requires a Muse Code subscription

name: Muse Ember
tagline: Meta's smallest, lowest-cost Muse model for the coding and agent steps that repeat all day
description: Muse Ember is the smallest and most efficient model in Meta's Muse family, introduced on November 9, 2026. It is built for the work agents repeat many times a session: tool calls, coding subtasks such as reading files and running tests, routing, extraction, and long document parsing. It takes text, images, audio, and video as input, has a 1M-token context window with up to 512K output tokens, and supports the Responses API. Meta suggests pairing it with Muse Wonder, which plans the hardest problems while Muse Ember handles the volume. It is the first model Meta trained using Muse Wonder Full, and it is available as muse-ember-1.0 in Muse Code and on the Meta Model API, as well as on Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud.
bestFor: low-cost subagents in a coding harness
tool calls, routing, and data extraction at high volume
pricingNote: Meta Model API: $0.10 per million input tokens, $0.004 per million cached input tokens, and $0.50 per million output tokens for prompts up to 200K tokens; longer prompts cost $0.30 input and $1.50 output per million

name: Claude Duet
tagline: Anthropic's proactive agent that briefs you, works in the background, and asks before acting
description: Claude Duet is a new app from Anthropic where Claude works as a proactive agent, opened as a research preview on October 21, 2026. Built around Claude Opus 5.5, it sends a short morning brief from your connected apps, checks them every few hours, and messages you only when something needs attention. It runs on its own cloud computer with a browser, so tasks keep going when your devices are off, and it can use the 6,000 plus connectors in the Claude Marketplace. It shows you exactly what it will do and waits for approval before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document, or deletes anything. Available on iOS, Android, and claude.ai by waitlist.
bestFor: daily briefs across email and calendar
pricingNote: Research preview by waitlist for US Pro and Max subscribers; included in the plan and uses its usage limits

name: Ideogram
tagline: Image generation with strong text rendering
description: Ideogram is known for generating images that include readable text, useful for posters, logos, and marketing graphics.
pricingNote: Free accounts get weekly credits; Plus $15, Pro $42, and Team $20 per user a month billed yearly ($20, $60, and $30 billed monthly); pay as you go credits at 1 cent each, including API use; Enterprise is custom

name: FLUX
tagline: Black Forest Labs image models
description: FLUX is a family of high-quality text-to-image models from Black Forest Labs, available via partners and APIs.
pricingNote: Pay as you go API credits (1 credit is $0.01), priced per image by model and resolution, with the same price in the API and the Playground and no subscriptions or seat fees; licenses for self-hosting the open weights are sold separately

name: Krea 3
tagline: Fast image editing that keeps products and characters consistent
description: Krea 3 is Krea's new image editing and generation model, released October 15, 2026, with its API opened to every workspace on October 19. Most edits finish in under 8 seconds at native 2K, it takes up to 6 reference images per edit, and it keeps products, labels, logos, characters, and text intact while changing the rest of the scene. It is the default image model in the Krea app and is also served through partners like fal, Replicate, Together AI, and OpenRouter.
pricingNote: Free Krea plan with a daily compute allowance; paid Basic, Pro, and Max plans on krea.ai; API $0.06 per 2K image and $0.03 per 1K image

name: Seedream 5.5
tagline: ByteDance image model with stable multi-round editing and transparent-background output
description: Seedream 5.5 is the image creation model from ByteDance's Seed team, introduced on November 9, 2026. It keeps unedited regions unchanged at the pixel level, so you can keep editing the same image across 100 rounds without color shifts or detail loss. It also generates native RGBA images with full and partial transparency, so assets come out ready to drop into a layout without background removal, and it improves photo realism and the rendering of dense, small text. At launch it is available in the Doubao, Doubao Work, and Jimeng apps, with API access on Volcano Engine Ark announced as coming soon. ByteDance says a Pro version of the 5.5 series will follow.
bestFor: editing one image over many rounds
images with dense or small text
pricingNote: Available in the Doubao, Doubao Work, and Jimeng apps; API on Volcano Engine Ark announced but not live as of November 9, 2026, so check the official site for current pricing

name: ReSO AI
tagline: GEO and AI search visibility for brands
description: ReSO AI helps brands track and improve how they show up in AI search answers and generative engines. Useful for teams focused on GEO and AI visibility rather than classic SEO alone.
pricingNote: See official site for pricing

name: Leonardo AI
tagline: Creative AI image and asset platform
description: Leonardo AI offers image generation, fine-tuned models, and creative asset tools for games, design, and marketing.
pricingNote: Free plan with 150 fast tokens a day (free creations are public); Essential $12, Premium $30, and Ultimate $60 a month, with up to 20% off billed yearly; Premium and Ultimate add unlimited relaxed image generation on select models; team plans from $24 per seat a month; pay as you go API

name: Adobe Firefly
tagline: Adobe's commercially safer generative AI
description: Adobe Firefly generates images and design effects inside Adobe apps, trained with an emphasis on commercial use considerations.
pricingNote: Free use with limited daily generations; paid Firefly Standard, Pro, Pro Plus, and Premium plans include 2,000, 4,000, 10,000, and 50,000 monthly credits for premium features plus unlimited standard image generations; Creative Cloud Pro includes 4,000 credits

name: Canva
tagline: Design platform with AI for graphics, social posts, and presentations
description: Canva is a browser and mobile design platform for social graphics, presentations, videos, documents, and print, with templates, brand kits, and built-in AI through Canva AI. On October 29, 2026, Canva announced Canva Brush, a vision-language model for design built by its Canva Research lab. Brush handles supported design edits in Canva AI: it can restyle images, make changes across a multi-page design, and remix an asset into another format, such as turning a slide into an Instagram graphic, and everything it makes stays editable. Canva says Brush is up to 69% faster for general design edits and 46% lower in cost per edit than its previous design agent. It is available to Canva Pro subscribers by choosing Brush in the Canva AI model menu, with wider availability coming soon. A week earlier Canva launched Canva Craft, its first image generation model.
bestFor: presentations and brand kits for small teams
pricingNote: Canva Free for anyone; paid Pro Lite, Pro (one person, 10x more AI use than Free), and Business (small teams, 20x more AI use, plus team tools) plans with a free trial; optional AI Pass add-on; free Canva for Nonprofits for one team of up to 50; prices vary by region on canva.com/pricing

name: Topaz Labs
tagline: AI upscaling and photo repair, now with the all-in-one Wonder 4 model
description: Topaz Labs makes AI image and video enhancement software, including desktop apps and the browser-based Topaz for Web. In its November 2026 release, published November 3, Topaz for Web added Wonder 4, an all-in-one mixture-of-experts model that upscales and repairs an image in a single pass: it handles upscaling, denoising, deblurring and sharpening, compression-artifact removal, and face recovery without manual settings. The same release added Image HDR, which turns standard images into HDR versions with a gain map. At launch Wonder 4 is available in Topaz for Web.
bestFor: repairing old, blurry, or compressed photos
one-click photo enhancement in the browser
pricingNote: Topaz for Web Image is $12 a month on a limited-time sale (normally $19) or $109 a year (normally $199); Topaz Studio with every app is $69 a month, $45 a month on an annual commitment, or $399 a year; personal plans allow commercial use only for organizations under $1M in annual revenue

name: Kling AI
tagline: AI video generation from Kuaishou
description: Kling AI generates video from text and images with competitive motion quality for short-form creative clips. Paid plans add professional mode, watermark removal, video extension, and higher monthly credit allotments.
pricingNote: Free Basic plan with login credits; Standard $79.20 a year (660 credits a month); Pro $293.04 a year (3,000 credits a month); Premier from $728.64 a year (8,000 credits a month); monthly renewals and higher Premier tiers on klingai.com/membership

name: Google Veo 3.1
tagline: Google DeepMind's video model with native sound and dialogue
description: Veo 3.1 is Google DeepMind's leading video generation model, first released in October 2025 and added to BuildStack to fill a gap in the video list. It generates sound effects, ambient noise, and dialogue together with the picture, follows reference images of a character, object, or style, extends a clip from its last second, and builds transitions between a first and last frame, with camera controls and output in 1080p or 4K. Videos made with Veo carry a SynthID watermark. You can use it in Google Flow, which offers Veo 3.1 Lite, Fast, and Quality modes, and developers can build with it on Google's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.
bestFor: short video clips with sound and dialogue
keeping a character consistent across shots
image-to-video with first and last frames
pricingNote: Every Google Flow account gets 50 free credits a day: a Veo 3.1 Lite video uses 10 credits, Fast 20, and Quality 100 (Lite and Fast cost half on Ultra); Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra add monthly credits, and free users may be unable to generate video at peak hours

name: Gemini Omni Flash
tagline: Google's video model you can create and edit by conversation
description: Gemini Omni Flash is Google's conversational video model family. It turns mixes of text, images, video, and voice into short videos you can edit by chat while keeping characters consistent. On November 5, 2026 Google added Omni 1.2 Flash to Google Vids, with up to three 15-second videos a month at no cost for anyone with a Google account. The developer model gemini-omni-1.1-flash remains in the Gemini API (3 to 10 second clips, extension, first/last frame, 360p to 4K). Videos carry a SynthID watermark.
bestFor: short AI videos from mixed references
editing a generated video by chat
Veo replacement in the Gemini API
pricingNote: Included with Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra in the Gemini app and Flow; up to three 15-second Omni 1.2 Flash videos a month at no cost in Google Vids for anyone with a Google account; no cost in YouTube Shorts and YouTube Create; API billed per Gemini API pricing

name: Seedance 2.5
tagline: ByteDance Seed video model with audio and 30-second takes
description: Seedance 2.5 is the video creation model from ByteDance's Seed team. It generates audio and video together in clips of up to 30 seconds per pass, supports multiple rounds of extension for multi-minute stories, takes up to 30 images, 10 video clips, and 10 audio clips as references in one pass, and offers timestamp-level editing plus green screen and camera perspective edits. It is available in Jimeng AI and Doubao, with API access through BytePlus ModelArk.
bestFor: longer AI video with synced audio
editing specific moments in a clip
pricingNote: Available in Jimeng AI and Doubao apps; API via BytePlus ModelArk; see official site

name: Pika H3 Flex
tagline: Fast open-weight video model with synced audio and up to 12 references
description: Pika H3 Flex is Pika's post-trained version of the MiniMax H3 video model, released October 29, 2026. It generates video with synchronized stereo audio at 480p or 768p in six steps instead of 50, and Pika says a 15-second 768p clip can take as little as seven seconds of model compute. You can combine up to 12 reference images, videos, and audio files in one generation, edit parts of a shot while keeping the performance, and upscale a chosen clip to 1080p, 2K, or 4K. Through the Pika API you can also get separate dialogue, music, and effect audio stems as WAV files. The generator weights and inference code are released for you to run on your own hardware.

A voice agent SDK built on LiveKit combines listening, reasoning, tool calling, and speaking in one streaming pipeline, over SIP or WebRTC. It runs on Mistral's EU, US, or global API or on your own infrastructure.

In October it also added Nova-3 Medical Multilingual for medical audio in 10 languages. Other options include Flux for real-time speech recognition in voice agents, speaker diarization, smart formatting, and keyterm prompting, plus Flux TTS and Aura-2 text-to-speech and a Voice Agent API. Billing is per second with no rounding up, there is a dedicated EU endpoint, and Enterprise customers can self-host or sign a HIPAA BAA.

name: AssemblyAI-TTS-1
tagline: Low-latency text to speech built for voice agents

It ships with more than 4,000 voices, instant voice cloning once you confirm the speaker's permission, word timestamps, and a choice of US or EU processing. At launch it speaks English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, and Portuguese, and AssemblyAI provides reference agents for LiveKit and Pipecat.

It handles interruptions and turn-taking on noisy lines, speaks more than 50 languages with switching mid-conversation in the same voice, and pronounces URLs, emails, and codes accurately. You build on it with the API, TypeScript and Python SDKs, a CLI, or a no-code agent builder, and Phonic offers SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA with a BAA, and zero data retention.

The updated 470M Turbo CTC model adds multilingual transcription with native punctuation and runs about 1.6 times faster than before, and the refreshed 4.1 2B Plus model improves speaker attribution and timestamps for meetings and calls. Because it is promptable, it can also answer questions about audio and return word timestamps. NVIDIA reports it ranks first among open-weight models on the Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard for English at 5.33% word error rate. It is a Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts model with about 34B total and 4.3B active parameters that runs on one H100 80GB GPU, with FP8 and NVFP4 versions for local RTX and DGX Spark machines. It is built for recorded audio rather than live streaming.
